# Matthew D. Webb

<p class="research-line">Applied Microeconometrics <span>·</span> Causal Inference <span>·</span> Machine Learning and AI for Economic Measurement <span>·</span> Empirical Microeconomics</p>

I develop and apply econometric methods for credible empirical research, with a particular focus on inference with clustered data and difference-in-differences designs. My current work also uses machine learning and AI to measure economically meaningful features in images and other complex data. I am also a Co-Director of the [Centre for Economic Evidence on Migration (CEEM)](https://ceem.ca/) at Carleton University.

## Current Research

::: {.feature-grid}
::: {.feature-card}
### Good Controls Gone Bad: Difference-in-Differences with Covariates

Studies identification with time-varying covariates and introduces the Intersection Difference-in-Differences (DID-INT) estimator.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.14447) · [Software](software.qmd#did-int)
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Improved Inference for CSDID

Cluster-jackknife inference for modern difference-in-differences estimators.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2602.12043) · [Watch video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=8xLv7Bu-_l0)
:::

::: {.feature-card}
### Representation Risk in Pretrained Image Encoders

Studies how plausible choices of pretrained image encoders can lead to different predictions and conclusions, and how to assess representation risk.

[Paper](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.35470) · [Software](software.qmd#lookagain-ml) · [Watch video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dA8yxSYdpi8)
:::

:::

## Research Software

The [Software page](software.qmd) is a curated guide to implementations of my research methods across Stata, R, Julia, and Python. It groups software by method, gives verified installation commands, connects each implementation to its paper, and credits the implementation author.
